transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's a pleasure to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because I just can't keep my mind on one thing anymore. It's getting really frustrating. I'm a carpenter, and if just one saw starts up across the shop, or somebody walks past the office, or even if I just have a passing thought about another job we're doing... it pulls me right off what I’m working on. And then, before I know it, the whole day just gets away from me.
Have you struggled with this kind of distractibility and difficulty focusing your entire life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

It's been my whole life, really. It's definitely not a new thing. 

Even way back in grade school, well before I was 12, my teachers were always telling my mother that I was bright but just careless. I was always losing my homework, or... or forgetting instructions right after they gave them. I'd end up just staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. So, yeah, it's always been there.
